topic: From a proposed answer to a kept receipt

items.prompt: In the loop, which step can accept an answer?

choices.text: The local model, when it is confident

model.note: A model cannot reliably pick its own correct answer. No learned model sits on the step that accepts.

cache.note: The cache stores answers that already passed, and re-checks them before serving.

source.quote: Only the external check can accept an answer

items.prompt: A pass writes a receipt. What happens if one byte of it changes?

choices.text: The re-check still passes, since the answer was right
Nothing; the receipt is just a log

passes.note: The receipt is named by a fingerprint of its own contents. Change a byte and the fingerprint no longer matches.

nothing.note: The fingerprint is what makes the receipt re-checkable offline.

source.quote: a change to any byte makes that check fail

items.prompt: No candidate passes and the attempt budget runs out. What does Flywheel do?

choices.text: Names a stronger tier and leaves the call to you
Calls a stronger model by itself
Releases the best candidate with a warning

calls.note: The page says it never calls that tier for you.

releases.note: Only a pass writes a receipt. An answer that never passed is held back.

source.quote: It never calls that tier for you.

items.prompt: What does the proof cache do before it serves a stored answer again?

choices.text: Asks the model to confirm it

serves.note: Serving straight from memory would trust a stored answer without checking it again. The page says the cache does not do that.

asks.note: The model is not the judge. The re-check is the same external kind.

source.quote: the cache re-checks the answer before it serves it

items.prompt: What does the loop drawing not show?

order.note: The drawing does show the order of the steps. What it cannot show is an effect on accuracy.

decider.note: The drawing marks the deciding step with a bar. Its limit is accuracy: no measured uplift.

source.quote: It does not show that the loop raises accuracy.
